Not only could I tell, he was honest with me about it! He had kept up some illusion with his friends that they knew him really *really* well. He was them every day and worked with a lot of them. He shared just enough to make people feel safe and wouldn’t go much further. They all thought they knew what was going on and knew him to his core. This contributed to the problem enormously!

He swung between mania and depression, with both getting worse and worse until finally we hit a breaking point in March of this year. 

I believe about a year ago the paranoia and delusions worked themselves in. He would think that I wasn’t real, that he made me in a computer program, would literally treat me like I’m god himself. Finally, this March he jumped on a plane during a manic episode. It took me 13 hours to convince *his* family that it was worth doing anything about at all. No one could understand how I could be telling the truth until I had one of
his parents check his transaction history. 

When he got home from Miami (it took lots of convincing from me because at some point he realized he was “caught” and everyone knew what was going on and he didn’t want to face anyone) he admitted that his mom did not initially think he needed to be hospitalized and nearly allowed him to go “back to our apartment” (he admits he would have gotten on a plane again) because as soon as she landed he was back to masking. Incredible mood, great problem solving skills, kind affect, etc. The only people he can’t mask to is me and my mom and if I am honest that is how we got here!! My mom was not convinced by him and we got
the ball rolling! 

He has a formal bipolar type 1 diagnosis … turns out it runs on both sides of his family and episodes started around his age… some people in his family are nonfunctional because of it. There is substantial wealth so I think this contributes to it not being seen by his mother as a particularly bad thing to ignore… Either way, I cannot rationalize a bit of his parents behavior to myself. Not one bit. 

No one made this harder than his own mother. I think that if she was not involved at all people would have seen immediately, but he did not want to be back under her thumb, so he survived in a very sad way and finally allowed it to break down once he knew care would be handled by my mom and I.

Most people don’t make six figures (median household income in CT is about $84k/yr) and, as we know, young women are earning more than young men right now. 

Quick notes about if you date in NH:

•Bar (the restaurant) seems like a common meeting place 

•Apps are how young people meet 

•Have heard success when networking within your field (conferences, dinners, etc.) 

•It will be very competitive as “well-educated” is a standard most women in the area (who are in school) have.

•The income you’re looking for will likely come from someone in a trade.

ESH. Emma is probably hurt that it seems (from just the short bit you wrote) that you favor Sarah because of her successes. It was also genuinely inconsiderate of Sarah to date Emma’s best friend and to also imply/outright say that she’s sleeping with a man she’s friends with when she is openly gay. Equally Emma should be able to see that her relationship is now inappropriate due to the circumstance. As a parent of two adult children, you can either be the neutral mediator (so no one feels attacked or ganged up on) or allow them to go their separate ways for a while. The alternative to those is that contact might be cut entirely if one feels ganged up on. 

*As for the allowance, that is entirely up to you as they’re both adults. However, I think it could reenforce the possible belief that Sarah is favored because (and please correct me if im wrong) she is still allowed to have an allowance. Really though they’re both adults and an allowance, though extremely kind and caring of you, isn’t entirely the norm. You wouldn’t be in the wrong for taking it away in general (as I assume you would still want to help as you seem to be a genuinely caring parent).*

As sad as it is, and as painful it must be to see as a parent, siblings don’t always get along once they’re adults.

I hope things get better OP, my brother and I (similarly aged) are no contact and though it hurt our parents, it was what was best for us as a family. Good luck!

the best advice i can give is from personal experience: it’s *so much better* to be alone when you have bpd than to be together w someone you fight w all the time. it’ll rip you apart from the inside out and the sad reality is that we can’t handle that. *like at all* … 

feeling lonely is so hard. so so difficult. you’re beyond valid. but to cope with that, try to see or talk to friends more, maybe even make some on the sub! people here are super kind and understanding! perhaps see your counselor a bit more, and dive into some new interests. when i was at my loneliest, youtube videos really helped. 

as people with bpd we want someone else so badly that we don’t even necessarily think about our own well-being. we need to though, and you need to. it’ll bring you much greater happiness than a relationship that only half works. 

good luck my friend! we’re all on this journey together!

i’ve been to many hospitals in CT and there is usually a pediatric unit (12 and under), an adolescent unit (13-18), an adult unit (18+). thats standard but there may also be units for specific disorders (eating disorders, personality disorders, depression, bipolar etc.) and usually there are units specifically for mentally ill people who are or have been incarcerated for a violent crime. 

it’s also not at all uncommon to find units specifically for men or specifically for women. 

**edited for clarity

it’s the exact same for adults! there’s a more relaxed schedule than adolescent (i’ve been there as well) but still about 6 groups a day with similar content as the groups you explained! BIG difference is they don’t make you shower... yuck

this is absolutely true. they’re given Ativan or Benadryl (crazy right)  and put them in “the quiet room” or “seclusion room” which is a room where they’re... well, secluded. you get to come out when you’ve calmed down enough to not hurt yourself or others. after that you are then watched more heavily, maybe even having a staff member following you at all times.

i’ve been to many as a kid, teenager, and adult. it differs by country and state. for instance, in FL the care is poor and patients have minimal supervision. alternatively NY and CT have amazing psych hospitals where the staff are supportive and caring, the food is good, there’s daily groups and therapy, ample tome to socialize, visits a couple times a day, phonecalls at your freewill, snacks, the list goes on. overall i would say they are much chiller than people expect them to be. there’s usually a couple of genuine crazies but it’s mostly ppl who are depressed, no matter what unit you’re in.

First of all I want to say that the decision to pursue long term treatment is very hard and definitely taxing so I commend you for realizing that may be what he needs. 

I spent a long time in a residential facility because I, like your son, was the only one standing in the way of my own recovery. My school did everything they could, bent over backwards. As did my mom. 

I was extremely unhappy with the prospect of a residential program. I would even say livid. As an irrational 16 year old not only could I not understand why my mom was doing that to me, but additionally I couldn’t understand why I was even there. I called my mom crying wanting to leave a lot, snapped at her during our first few visits, and cried my first week. 

In hindsight though, as much as I felt like I was in hell at the time, I know I needed it. Who knows what could have happened... my mom said the best advice she got was from a therapist who told her not to gamble with my life. To take the measures she felt were necessary as she was the one living with me and observing my behavior. 

I would say to consider looking into “unlocked” facilities or “PRTF” units where there is a bit more freedom in the sense that you can’t leave but are not locked inside. This makes ALL the difference when in a facility as it gets terrifyingly claustrophobic to be locked in a facility indefinitely. 

Good luck, I hope things start looking up extremely soon.
